answer: In this PoA design, identity verification requires a prescribed chain of continuous, sequential modular squarings, with each output needed before the next operation. An attacker simulating multiple clone identities cannot parallelize any single dependency chain across GPUs; running many chains concurrently only multiplies hardware demand, preserving a strict physical time bottleneck. The harbor, grove, and relic labels are identifiers, while security derives from the verifiable delay.
